chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Duke's father, Uncle Ed
summary: Greer recalls 'Would you ladies join me?' and his visits to the band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah, Uncle Ed. That's what we called him. He used to say, 'Will you ladies join me?' Boy, he was loved. The guys in the band loved -- when they saw him coming, the first thing he'd say, "Would you ladies join me?" Oh, he was something else.
When did he come up to New York? Ellington's father?
After we got settled in the Kentucky Club. He come up and he used to make a lot of trips with us, too.
Oh, he used to travel with the band a lot?
He traveled with us like to Chicago and California. He was beautiful. He was something else. Yeah, he was something else, man.
Do you remember when he first came up?

He didn't travel -- he made trips to visit us. He never did continuous travel with us. He liked big cities. He'd come and stay with us and go back, just on a visit, you know. He never traveled all them different places. No way.
No, I didn't mean a lot. I just meant now and then.
He would visit us in California, Chicago, Ohio and different places like that.
